text:
B: Hi. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, got you. Darren.
B: Laura. Hi. Erm, so we just sort of chat for three minutes, I think.
A: Apparently. Not sure what they're after, to be honest, but go on. Did you finish that puzzle thing?
B: Most of it. I got stuck on the last couple of grids, the ones with the shapes. I ran out of time.
A: Same. Gave up on the last one, couldn't see it. Bit of a daft way to start, but there you go.
B: Yeah. So where are you, roughly?
A: Basingstoke. Brighton Hill.
B: Oh, really? I'm in Chineham.
A: No way. Small world. What d'you do then?
B: I'm a management accountant at a logistics company, on one of the estates out by the ring road. Monthly accounts, budgets for three depots, that sort of thing. It's month-end next week, so it's about to get a bit hectic.
A: Right. I'm on an estate too, the other side. I run a builders' merchant, branch manager. Nine in the yard, two on the counter.
B: Oh, okay. That's quite a lot of people.
A: Yeah. Had a delivery turn up two hours late this morning, so the yard was absolutely heaving. Trade lads stood about moaning, drivers moaning. So I'm a bit knackered, if I'm honest.
B: I bet. Do you do your own figures, or does head office do all that?
A: Bit of both. I do stock, shrinkage, all that. Head office does the quarterly review and picks it apart. You'd probably enjoy that bit more than me.
B: Ha, maybe. Usually I'm the one picking it apart, to be honest. Sorry.
A: Ha. Fair enough. Kids?
B: One, Alfie. He's six, Year 2. My mum does pick-up a couple of days, she's over in Tadley.
A: Funny. My lad's Alfie as well. He's nine. He's with his mum in Tadley, actually.
B: Oh, that's a coincidence. Two Alfies and Tadley.
A: Yeah. Er, I have him every other weekend and a night in the week. So... yeah.
B: That must be hard, the in-between bit.
A: It is what it is. I take him to Reading when I can, the football. He's more into it than I was at nine, to be fair.
B: My husband would get on with you then. He has the football on all the time and I sort of half watch.
A: Who's he support?
B: Erm, Reading, I think, mostly? He moans about them a lot.
A: Then he's definitely Reading. Everyone moans. Lost again Saturday. Owners don't have a clue.
B: That's exactly what he says.
A: Ha. Do you do anything at weekends then, or is it all kids' stuff?
B: I do parkrun on a Saturday, War Memorial Park. I'm on eighty-seven, I want to get to a hundred.
A: Eighty-seven? Blimey. My partner drags me to that now and again. I do weights, three mornings before work. Running kills my knee.
B: I'm not fast. About thirty-one minutes. It's more the routine, really, gets me out the house.
A: Thirty-one's alright. Better than me when I'm hanging off the back.
B: Well, if you come on a Saturday you can say hello.
A: Maybe. Kelly'll be made up if I volunteer to go for once.
B: Erm, what else... do you do the Friday takeaway thing as well? Everyone seems to.
A: Every Friday. Chicken madras, same place, never changes.
B: We're the same. I keep saying we should cut down and then it's Friday and—
A: And it's Friday, yeah. No chance.
